precepts.text: The Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected: that's the word you want to highlight, be rejected, of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
precepts.point: But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me. Churches don't read that; churches will look at that and go, no, we're not reading that in Sunday school. You know what it means further? You ain't going to just be able to do what you want to do. You was put on this earth to do what the Most High and Christ said, and if you don't do that, then there's no reason for you to live. He said, if you don't want to do what you were created for, bring him before me and end his existence.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“But his citizens hated him, and sent a message after him, saying, We will not have this man to reign over us.” Who hated him? Mark shows it: “the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.”

Rejected is the word to highlight. The elders, the chief priests and the scribes rejected him: back then it was the scribes and Pharisees and those that followed them who said, we will not have this man to reign over us.

Today there are no groups called scribes and Pharisees, but the same spirit is here. They are the Christians, they are the Muslims; they fall into this. They reject his reign, and at the end of the parable the King says what becomes of them: “But those mine enemies, which would not that I should reign over them, bring hither, and slay them before me.”

precepts.text: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod: letting you know whose manner they were following. They were not just hypocrites; they were following after the manner of the wicked.
precepts.point: Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the Sadducees.

note.label: Bitterness: The Hidden Leaven From Cain To Esau

precepts.why:
Christ warned in Matthew 16 to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and in Matthew 23 he said to do what they bid from Moses' seat, but not after their works. Whose works were they following? Mark tells it: “And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.”

The leaven of Herod. That lets you know whose manner they were following: they were following the white man, Esau. That is why he tells us to beware.

So their leaven was not just being hypocrites. They were following after the manner of the wicked. Leaven is an influence that spreads, and when the rulers of Israel took on Herod's leaven, it spread through them; they came to move in the same spirit as the wicked they served. That is the warning to us: do not take on the leaven of Herod, the spirit of Esau, while wearing the garments of Israel.

precepts.text: What shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? What do the celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their bodies, to Amalek.
precepts.point: The pastors are the new taskmasters, sent out by Esau with his doctrines, pulling up in the Benz while you walk to church in the cold to give him your last.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
Terence Crawford said there was not a number that could get him back in that ring, and then said for 100 million dollars you can have my soul. That nigger was dead serious; look at his eyes. That is a dangerous man: a man who would sell out his mama and his children and do anything for money. That is the result of 400 years with Esau, and he just said out loud what the majority of Black celebrities, rappers and singers think.

“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” Esau gives you whatever you want: all the riches, all the connections, all the power, wealth you can't run from. But in order to get it, you lose your own soul.

“Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?” What do these celebrities give in exchange for their souls? Their booty. They give it up, and Amalek takes it. Your Jay-Zs and 50 Cents, your Mariah Careys and Whitneys: they have to give in order to receive.

What are you going to stand for if everything is about money? You have no dignity and no morals. These are the results of the leaders of this people causing them to err, and of Black Christians led by them being destroyed. There are no laws with them, because they were taught the laws are done away with.

precepts.text: His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor.
precepts.point: Christ is the Counsellor, and his counsel is not found on the world's couch.

note.label: Kill Or Be Killed

precepts.why:
“For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?” He was so lustful and covetous for the petty things this world provides that he loses his soul: he does not get the kingdom. You had a million gazillion dollars and still could not pay your way into heaven. Then Christ says, “Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words”, and Isaiah shows who those words belong to.

“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor.” That child is Christ, and these are his titles. Stop right there: Counsellor. Christ is the ultimate counselor. The counsel for everything you are dealing with in this world, in this captivity, is already here in his words.

But you despise Christ's words, brothers and sisters. You don't even want to pick up your Bible and read four chapters, or pick up the precept packet to learn how to move this weapon. You are ashamed that Christ, the ultimate physician, has the fix for you. You can't get this counsel on a damn white man's couch. You can't go to Dr. Phil and expect him to fix your life. Them demons can't fix your life; they destroy homes. And Christ's counsel is free. How is it black people love free stuff, but when Christ gives it to you for free, you deny it?

Some purposely avoid the counselors in the truth because they have itching ears, and go to those as new as themselves, because they don't want to hear: fix your house, stop watching porn, delete the apps, get a flip phone, stop hanging with the same folks. Whoever is ashamed of the Counsellor's words, the laws, statutes and commandments, the blueprint to get out of this demonic land, Christ will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father.

precepts.text: Scripture uses trees to represent men.
precepts.point: Some of these trees are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men.

note.label: Genesis 2: Adam, the Chosen of the Most High

precepts.why:
Some of the trees in the garden are literal trees, and some of these trees represent men. The scriptures use trees that way: when Christ touched the blind man’s eyes, “he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.”

Keep that in mind reading “Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it.” Not every tree there is a plant.

precepts.text: The Son of man must suffer and be rejected of the elders, the chief priests, and scribes, the ones he came unto.
precepts.point: This five thousand disproves the Christian claim that the Jews all rejected Christ. He came unto his own, meaning the religious leaders, the builders, the chief priests and rulers whose job was to guide the nation, and only those upper echelons rejected him, while thousands of the people believed and were zealous of the law.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Christ said who would reject him: “the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.”

Rejected of the elders, the chief priests and the scribes. Those are the ones he came unto, the builders whose job was to guide the nation, and they are the ones who received him not. The people believed by the thousands.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.why: The citizens that hated him: who hated Christ? You hear Christians go, "He came unto his own and his own received him not." Shut up. That ain't talking about all the Israelites. “And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes,” That's who hated Christ. That's who rejected him.
